gap: No result ChatGPT got states that 'Kestrel Tab-Tension 3' covers two surfaces with opposite projector compatibility. Elite lists the CineWhite version (1.1 gain, 180°) for ultra-short-throw, short-throw, standard-throw and triple-laser projectors. It lists the CineGrey 4D version (1.1 gain, 70°, 63% ambient light rejection) as 'Not Compatible With Ultra-short/Short Throw or Triple Laser Projectors'.
standout_why: I compared against projector-screen-guide.com/floor-rising-projector-screen, projectorverdict.com/best/best-motorized-projector-screen and primeareviews.com/guide/best-floor-rising-projector-screen. ProjectorVerdict already says the Kestrel TT3 CineGrey 4D (126 in, $1,923) is 'listed for standard long throw'. Projector-screen-guide already says the Kestrel TT2 CLR3 is UST-only. So the rivals have half of the finding. None of them sets the two TT3 surfaces side by side under one name, and ChatGPT's own card ('Kestrel Tab-Tension3 122in matte white … multiple throw types', $1,923) mixes up the two. My main target was the height from the floor to the bottom of the picture when the screen is fully raised, because that decides where a UST projector has to sit. None of the three rivals gives it for any model, but I could not source it either (see unsourced). That is why this scores 1, not 2 or 3.
decides: If the shopper has a UST projector, the Kestrel to consider is the CineWhite TT3 or the TT2 CLR3, never the TT3 CineGrey 4D. The 1.1-gain grey ALR version is for standard throw only. The choice for a UST in a lit room stays a UST-specific surface such as the VIVIDSTORM S PRO or AWOL ALR-F220C. Elite and VIVIDSTORM print the same kind of spec on different bases (Elite's 180° vs 70° next to VIVIDSTORM's 170°), so those numbers should not be compared directly.
